ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square, and inside and outside it there are four symmetric lens-shaped regions, respectively located on the upper, lower, left, and right four sides of the square. In each lens-shaped region there is a gray circle; the center of the gray circle is on one side of the square; these gray circles are tangent to semicircular arcs whose centers are the corner points. The figure is horizontally and vertically symmetric about the center of the square, so the four gray circles are congruent. Reasoning: It is only necessary to find the area of one gray circle, then multiply by 4. Let the side length of the square be 2, and place it in the coordinate system [-1,1] × [-1,1], with the center of the square O=(0,0). Consider the upper gray circle. The centers of the two relevant upper semicircles are the two upper corner points of the square A=(-1,1), B=(1,1). These semicircles pass through O, so the semicircle radius R=AO=BO=√(1^2+1^2)=√2. Let the center of the upper gray circle be T=(x,1), and the radius be r. Because the gray circle is internally tangent to the two semicircular arcs, AT=BT=R-r. Also because A, T, and B are all on the upper side y=1, AT=x+1, BT=1-x. From AT=BT, obtain x=0, so T is the midpoint of the upper side, and AT=BT=1. Therefore 1=R-r, giving r=√2-1. The area of one gray circle is πr^2=π(√2-1)^2=π(3-2√2). The total area of the four gray circles is 4π(3-2√2).

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, the square has side length 2. The semi-circles pass through the midpoint of the square and have their centres on the corners of the square. The grey circles have their centres on the sides of the square and touch the semi-circles. How big is the total area of the grey parts?

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: it shows a square of side 2 with four congruent grey circles, one centered on each side of the square; each grey circle sits inside the lens-shaped region formed by two semicircular arcs whose centers are the adjacent corners of the square. Solve one grey circle and multiply by 4. Put the square as [-1,1] x [-1,1], so its midpoint is O=(0,0). The upper two relevant semicircles have centers at the upper corners A=(-1,1) and B=(1,1), and since they pass through O, their radius is R=sqrt(1^2+1^2)=sqrt(2). Let the top grey circle have center T=(x,1) on the top side and radius r. Because it touches both upper semicircular arcs internally, AT=BT=R-r. Since A,T,B are collinear on the top side, AT=x+1 and BT=1-x, so x=0 and AT=BT=1. Thus r=R-1=sqrt(2)-1. The total grey area is 4*pi*r^2=4*pi*(sqrt(2)-1)^2=4*pi*(3-2sqrt(2)).
